title: 第75章 医道大会第76章 挑衅
lines: 秦川入谷第十六天，百草谷迎来了三年一度的医道大会。
这场盛会是中界医道宗门的最高规格集会，各大医道宗门都会派出代表团参加，展示各自的医道成果、交流医术心得，同时也是一场暗流涌动的势力博弈。今年的主办方是百草谷，会场设在谷口的演武场——那是百草谷唯一一块足够容纳上千人的开阔区域，平时用来考核弟子的灵针术和药浴术，现在被临时改造成了会场。
苏木槿提前两天给秦川送来了一份参会宗门的名单，简要介绍了各宗的背景。她告诉他，天医宗今年的代表团团长是少宗主柳玄——天医宗宗主柳南山的独子，年仅一百二十岁就已是化神期修士，医术在中界年轻一代中罕有对手。此人医术极高，但心气也极高，从不把凡人放在眼里。他曾在公开场合说过“凡人用凡药，修士用灵药，这是天道定数”，柳玄对凡人的态度，代表着天医宗一贯的立场。
秦川在脑中快速做了标注：柳玄代表的是整个修士阶层对凡人医疗的傲慢。这个傲慢不来自恶意，而来自认知惯性。但惯性越深，打破惯性时反弹越强。
医道大会开了三天。前两天秦川没有出席，他把时间花在工作间里继续整理凡人医药手册，沈青黛每天下午都会跑来告诉他当天的见闻。到了第三天，薛忘忧派人请秦川以“特别嘉宾”的身份出席。苏木槿来传话时特意提醒了他一句：“谷主安排你坐长老席。”
长老席是会场最前排靠右的位置，紧挨着针堂和药堂的长老团。秦川走到自己的座位前时，已经能感觉到来自四面八方的目光。一个穿着灰色布衣的凡人，坐在一群穿着长老袍、修为至少是元婴期的修士中间——这个画面本身就是在挑战某种默认的秩序。他旁边那位针堂长老倒是客气，对他点了点头。但另一侧的药堂长老连看都没看他一眼。
大会最后一天的压轴环节是“质疑与应答”，规则是由在场任意宗门的代表向主办方提出医学上的质疑，主办方必须当场回答。薛忘忧是主办方代表，但他没有亲自上台，而是将主位交给了百草谷医道院的首席教授韩松。
前三轮质疑都是常规的学术争论，围绕着灵针术的深浅、丹药的配比、药浴的火候展开，秦川听得很仔细，但始终没有开口。直到第四轮，柳玄站了起来。
天医宗少宗主穿着天蓝色的锦袍，腰悬玉剑，玉冠束发，面容俊朗。他走到质疑席站定，目光扫过百草谷的长老席，然后开口。
“百草谷近年标榜‘医道济世’，但据我所知，谷中最近收了一个凡人，让他在藏书阁自由翻阅医典，甚至让他在大讲堂给弟子做报告——讲什么‘凡人医学’。”他将“凡人医学”四个字咬得很慢，像是在品一道味道古怪的药引，“谷主可否解释一下——一个凡人，未经考核，没有修为，凭什么给修士讲课？”
全场安静下来。数百道目光齐刷刷地转向长老席，落在秦川身上。
秦川没有动，也没有低头。他感到苏木槿在侧后方微微倾身，但他用眼神示意她不要动。
薛忘忧正要开口，秦川提前一秒站了起来。
“柳公子，在下就是那个凡人。”他说，“谷主让我来回答这个问题。”
柳玄的眼神落在秦川身上，上下打量了一遍。那目光很平静，没有鄙夷，没有愤怒，只是一种俯视——像是鹰在看田鼠。
“你就是秦川？”
“好。那我问你——你有什么资格坐在长老席？”
秦川没有回答，而是反问：“柳公子，贵宗的《天医经》中，是否记载着一种以凡人之躯容纳天道之力而不死的功法？”
柳玄的眉头微不可察地跳了一下。
秦川继续说：“那篇功法在《天医经》第七卷末尾，名为‘凡躯承天法’。它的开篇第一句话是——‘凡人之身，无灵无脉，然其命门之火，通于天心。’这篇功法的理论基础是——凡人的身体虽然没有灵力，但命门穴是天生的天道感应点。你们的祖师写下了这篇功法，但从未有人练成。为什么？”
柳玄没有回答。但他的手不自觉地握紧了玉剑剑柄。
“因为没有凡人能承受天道之力。这句话不是否定凡人的价值——恰恰相反，你们的祖师认为凡人的命门能够承受天道之力，只是方法还没找到。你们祖师承认了凡人的可能性，而你们——把这篇功法封在经书末尾，一千年没人提起。”
秦川没有提高音量，也没有加任何情绪。他只是陈述事实。
“柳公子，我不需要修为也可以坐在这里。因为我做的是你们放弃了的事。”
全场寂静。
柳玄沉默了数息，然后缓缓开口：“你知道《天医经》第七卷非内门弟子不得翻阅。你怎么知道那篇功法的内容？”
“我看过。”秦川说，“百草谷的藏书阁里有一册《天医经总纲》，是贵宗第三代宗主送给百草谷的。那册总纲虽然不载功法全文，但包含了所有篇目提要。凡躯承天法——就在提要里。”
他说的是真话。那册《天医经总纲》是他在藏书阁二层无意间翻到的，当时他只是出于好奇翻了几页，没想到今天会派上用场。信息差的本质不是知道得比别人多，而是知道的东西在关键时刻恰好能用上。
柳玄盯着他看了很久，然后做出了一个出乎所有人意料的举动——他拱手，行了一个平辈之间的见面礼。不是晚辈对前辈的礼，不是修士对凡人的礼，而是平辈之间最简短的拱手。然后他转身走回天医宗的席位，坐下，没有再开口。
全场在短暂的寂静后，忽然爆发出一阵压抑不住的窃窃私语。秦川感到身边那位针堂长老侧过头看了他一眼，眼神里有种不加掩饰的诧异。另一位药堂长老捻着胡须没有说话，但嘴角似乎微微动了一下，像是在重新衡量秦川的分量。
苏木槿在侧后方无声地松了口气。她站的位置恰好能看到秦川的侧脸——他的表情很平静，没有胜利的得意，没有被挑衅后的愤怒，只是平静。就像他在青山村劈柴时一样——劈完一块，捡起来码好，继续下一块。
大会结束后，秦川独自走回竹楼。他没有觉得自己赢了什么——柳玄不是敌人，他只是这个时代修士认知模式的产物。天医宗的祖师曾经相信凡人有无限可能，但后人把这份相信封存在经书末尾，一千年没人翻阅。这不是柳玄的问题，是整个中界认知体系的问题。
他推开竹门，在工作簿上写下一行笔记：“柳玄——天医宗少宗主——化神期——医术精湛但对凡人认知有盲区——存在打破认知惯性的可能。”
写完他搁下笔。窗外月光清冷，远处演武场的灯火还未完全熄灭，偶尔有弟子匆匆走过药田间的小径，脚步声轻而急促。
他摸了摸怀里那块磨刀石。粗砺的表面硌着指腹，很熟悉，很踏实。然后他翻开《凡人医药手册》的草稿，继续写今天该写的那一页。
content_en:
On the sixteenth day after Qinchuan entered the valley, Baicao Valley ushered in the triennial medical conference.
This grand event is the highest-level gathering of the medical sects in the Central Realm. All major medical sects will send delegations to participate to showcase their respective medical achievements and exchange medical experience. It is also an undercurrent of power competition. This year's organizer is Baicao Valley, and the venue is located at the martial arts field at the entrance of the valley - it is the only open area in Baicao Valley that is large enough to accommodate thousands of people. The spiritual needle technique and medicinal bathing technique, which are usually used to assess the disciples, have been temporarily transformed into the venue.
Su Mujin sent Qin Chuan a list of participating sects two days in advance and briefly introduced the background of each sect. She told him that the leader of Tianyi Sect’s delegation this year was the young sect leader Liu Xuan, the only son of Liu Nanshan, the master of Tianyi Sect. At only 120 years old, he was already a monk in the transformation stage of the gods, and his medical skills were rarely rivaled among the younger generation in the middle world. This person has extremely high medical skills, but also a very high-spirited spirit, and never takes ordinary people seriously. He once said in public that "Mortals use ordinary medicines, while monks use spiritual medicines. This is the decree of heaven." Liu Xuan's attitude towards mortals represents the consistent stance of the Heavenly Medicine Sect.
Qin Chuan quickly made a note in his mind: Liu Xuan represents the arrogance of the entire monk class towards mortal medical care. This arrogance does not come from malice, but from cognitive inertia. But the deeper the inertia is, the stronger the rebound will be when it is broken.
The medical conference was held for three days. Qin Chuan did not attend the first two days. He spent his time in the workshop and continued to compile the mortal medicine manual. Shen Qingdai would come every afternoon to tell him what he had seen that day. On the third day, Xue Wangyou sent someone to invite Qin Chuan to attend as a "special guest". When Su Mujin came to deliver the message, she reminded him specifically: "The Valley Master has arranged for you to sit at the elder's table."
The elders' seat is the right-hand position in the front row of the venue, next to the elders of the Acupuncture Hall and the Medicine Hall. When Qin Chuan walked to his seat, he could already feel the eyes from all directions. A mortal dressed in gray cloth sits among a group of monks wearing elder robes whose cultivation is at least the Nascent Soul stage - this image itself challenges a certain default order. The elder of Needle Hall next to him was polite and nodded to him. But the elder of the medicine hall on the other side didn't even look at him.
The grand finale of the conference on the last day is "Question and Answer". The rule is that a representative of any sect present may raise a medical question to the organizer, and the organizer must answer it on the spot. Xue Wangyou was the representative of the organizer, but he did not go on stage in person. Instead, he handed the chair to Han Song, the chief professor of Baicaogu Medical Hospital.
The first three rounds of questioning were all conventional academic debates, centering on the depth of spiritual acupuncture, the ratio of elixirs, and the heat of medicinal baths. Qin Chuan listened carefully, but never spoke. It wasn't until the fourth round that Liu Xuan stood up.
The young master of the Tianyi Sect is wearing a sky blue brocade robe, with a jade sword hanging from his waist, a jade crown binding his hair, and a handsome face. He walked to the questioning seat and stood there, glancing at the elders' seat in Baicao Valley, and then spoke.
"Baicao Valley has boasted of 'medicine to help the world' in recent years, but as far as I know, the valley has recently accepted a mortal and allowed him to browse medical classics freely in the library. He even asked him to give a report to the disciples in the lecture hall - about 'mortal medicine'." He chewed the words "mortal medicine" very slowly, as if he was tasting a strange medicinal introduction, "Master of the valley, can you explain - why should a mortal, without examination and cultivation, give lectures to monks?"
The whole place fell silent. Hundreds of eyes turned to the elders' table and fell on Qin Chuan.
Qin Chuan did not move or lower his head. He felt Su Muzhen leaning slightly from the side, but he used his eyes to signal her not to move.
Just as Xue Wangyou was about to speak, Qin Chuan stood up a second earlier.
"Young Master Liu, I am that mortal." He said, "The Valley Master asked me to answer this question."
Liu Xuan's eyes fell on Qin Chuan and he looked up and down. The gaze was calm, not contemptuous, not angry, just looking down - like a hawk looking at a field mouse.
"Are you Qin Chuan?"
"Yes."
"Okay. Then let me ask you - what qualifications do you have to sit at the elders' table?"
Qin Chuan did not answer, but asked: "Mr. Liu, does Guizong's "Heavenly Medicine Sutra" record a technique that allows a mortal body to contain the power of heaven and survive?"
Liu Xuan's brows jumped slightly.
Qin Chuan continued: "That exercise is at the end of the seventh volume of the "Heavenly Medicine Sutra" and is called 'Mortal Body Carrying Heaven's Method'. The first sentence of its opening chapter is - 'The mortal body has no soul and no veins, but the fire of its Mingmen is connected to the heart of heaven.' The theoretical basis of this exercise is - although the mortal body has no spiritual power, the Mingmen acupoint is a natural induction point for the way of heaven. Your ancestor wrote this exercise, but no one has ever practiced it. Why?"
Liu Xuan didn't answer. But his hand unconsciously clenched the hilt of the jade sword.
"Because no mortal can withstand the power of heaven. This sentence does not deny the value of mortals - on the contrary, your ancestors believed that mortals' life gates can withstand the power of heaven, but the method has not yet been found. Your ancestors recognized the possibility of mortals, and you - sealed this technique at the end of the book, and no one mentioned it for a thousand years."
Qin Chuan did not raise his voice or add any emotion. He just states the facts.
"Young Master Liu, I don't need any cultivation to sit here. Because I am doing what you have given up on."
There was silence.
Liu Xuan was silent for a few breaths, and then slowly spoke: "You know that the seventh volume of the "Heavenly Medicine Sutra" is not allowed to be read by non-inner disciples. How do you know the content of that article?"
"I have seen it," Qin Chuan said. "There is a volume of "The General Outline of the Heavenly Medicine Sutra" in the library of Baicao Valley, which was given to Baicao Valley by the third-generation head of your sect. Although the general outline does not contain the full text of the exercises, it does contain the summary of all the chapters. The method of inheriting the heaven through the mortal body - it is in the summary."
He told the truth. He accidentally opened the "General Outline of the Heavenly Medicine Sutra" on the second floor of the library. At that time, he just flipped through a few pages out of curiosity, but he didn't expect that it would come in handy today. The essence of information gap is not to know more than others, but that what you know happens to be useful at critical moments.
Liu Xuan stared at him for a long time, and then made a move that was beyond everyone's expectations - he held his hand in a meeting ceremony between peers. It is not a courtesy from a junior to a senior, nor a courtesy from a monk to a mortal, but the briefest hand-over between peers. Then he turned around and walked back to the seat of Tianyi Sect, sat down, and didn't speak again.
After a brief silence, the whole place suddenly erupted into a burst of uncontrollable whispers. Qin Chuan felt the needle hall elder next to him turned his head and glanced at him, with undisguised surprise in his eyes. Another medicine hall elder twirled his beard and said nothing, but the corners of his mouth seemed to move slightly, as if he was re-evaluating Qin Chuan's weight.
Su Muxin let out a silent sigh of relief from behind. She stood just in a position where she could see Qin Chuan's profile - his expression was calm, without the pride of victory or anger after being provoked, just calm. Just like when he was chopping firewood in Qingshan Village - after chopping a piece, he picked it up and stacked it before moving on to the next piece.
After the meeting, Qin Chuan walked back to the bamboo building alone. He didn't feel that he had won anything - Liu Xuan was not an enemy, he was just a product of the cognitive model of monks in this era. The founder of the Heavenly Medicine Sect once believed that mortals have infinite possibilities, but later generations sealed this belief at the end of the scriptures, and no one read it for a thousand years. This is not Liu Xuan's problem, but the entire Zhongjie cognitive system's problem.
He pushed open the bamboo door and wrote a line of notes on the workbook: "Liu Xuan—the young master of the Heavenly Medicine Sect—in the stage of becoming a god—has superb medical skills but has a blind spot in cognition of mortals—there is the possibility of breaking the cognitive inertia."
After he finished writing, he put down his pen. The moonlight outside the window was cold and cold, and the lights of the martial arts field in the distance had not been completely extinguished. Occasionally, disciples hurriedly walked through the paths among the medicine fields, and their footsteps were light and hasty.
He touched the whetstone in his arms. The rough surface rubs against the fingertips, feeling familiar and at ease. Then he opened the draft of "Mortal Medicine Manual" and continued writing the page he should write today.
